author: product-requirements-expert
title: Veterinarian directory can be narrowed to one specialty
summary: Both the veterinarian directory page and its machine-readable form accept an optional specialty named in the request and list only the veterinarians holding it; naming none leaves both surfaces exactly as they are today.
acceptance_criteria: REQ-VET-004: given a specialty some veterinarians hold, when the directory page is requested with specialty=<name>, then only those veterinarians are listed, still a page at a time.
REQ-VET-004: given a specialty some veterinarians hold, when the machine-readable list is requested with specialty=<name>, then only those veterinarians come back, in one response.

REQ-VET-004: given a named specialty differing from the held specialty only by letter case, when either surface is requested, then it matches; matching is on the whole specialty name, so only part of a name matches nothing.

REQ-VET-004: given a specialty no veterinarian holds, when either surface is requested, then the normal page or document comes back with an empty veterinarian list and HTTP 200 - not 404 and not an error.

REQ-VET-004: given a specialty value that is empty or spaces alone, when either surface is requested, then the surface behaves as though the parameter were absent, the same convention the empty owner search follows.
REQ-VET-004: given a narrowed directory spanning more than one page, when the reader follows a pagination link, then the link carries the specialty and the next page stays narrowed.
REQ-VET-004: given no specialty parameter, when either surface is requested, then behavior is unchanged from today, including page size and the total counts shown.

REQ-VET-003: given the clinic's veterinarians, when the machine-readable list is requested, then every veterinarian and their specialties come back in one response - the surface is supported, no longer an unclaimed artifact.
non_goals: A form, dropdown, or any other page control for choosing a specialty - the narrowing is requested through the URL only. A visible control is a possible follow-up request, not part of this slice.
Free-text search over veterinarians, pets, or visits - NG-9 still bars it.
Narrowing by more than one specialty at once.
Managing veterinarians or specialties through the application - NG-2 is untouched.
notes: Two requirement ids ship in this one slice: REQ-VET-003 (the machine-readable veterinarian list is a supported surface again) needs no production change beyond coverage, so it batches with REQ-VET-004 rather than taking a slice of its own. The withdrawn REQ-VET-002 stays withdrawn and its id is not reused. NG-9 narrowed 2026-08-26 - docs/adr/2026-08-26-non-goal-vet-search-narrowed.md. New behavior must be covered by tests. The ADR index table in docs/adr/README.md still needs the 2026-08-26 non-goal row; that file is outside the product-requirements-expert write scope.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The slice is a second instance of a pattern the codebase already runs: a Spring Data derived query narrowing a listing, paged by the controller's private pagination helper (OwnerRepository.findByLastNameStartingWith + OwnerController.findPaginatedForOwnersLastName). No new package, no new type, no new integration, no service layer introduced. system-design.md Contracts already carries VetRepository/VetController/Vets; the adjustment is a parameter on each. One point needed a decision rather than a lookup - how a caller-supplied query value interacts with the @Cacheable("vets") repository, whose cache has no size limit and no eviction (Open Questions #5). That is recorded in a new ADR because the resulting rule is imperative and the ADR back-link rule requires a record; it is a bounded adjustment, not new design ground, so the verdict stays minor. REQ-VET-003 needs no production change at all - the /vets route already exists; it is a status change already made in the PRD plus test coverage, and system-design.md's Known Defects row calling that route requirement-less is now removed.
integration_points: VetRepository gains two narrowed reads - one returning Page<Vet> for the HTML surface, one returning Collection<Vet> for the JSON surface - alongside the two existing findAll methods, which are unchanged.

VetController.showVetList and VetController.showResourcesVetList each gain an optional specialty @RequestParam; both normalize it through one shared private helper so the two surfaces cannot drift on blank-handling.
vetList.html pagination links gain the specialty; the HTML model gains an attribute carrying the current specialty so the template can rebuild the links.
Vets is unchanged - it wraps whatever list the route produces, narrowed or not, so the JSON root element shape is identical either way. No DTO is introduced.

patterns.description: Paged derived query narrowing a listing by a request value - the pattern the specialty query instantiates. Matching semantics differ deliberately: StartingWith there, whole-name IgnoreCase equality here, per REQ-VET-004.
The blank-parameter convention to mirror: a null or whitespace-only value is stripped and then treated as no search at all. Mirror the convention, not the mechanism - see the first risk.

addPaginationModel already derives totalPages/totalItems from the Page it is handed, so the displayed counts narrow with the list once the narrowed Page is passed in. It needs only the extra specialty model attribute.

risks.risk: OwnerController's blank convention is mirrored mechanically: pass an empty string to the narrowed query the way OwnerController passes one to findByLastNameStartingWith. An empty prefix matches every owner; an empty whole-name equality matches no vet, so a blank specialty would return an empty directory instead of the full one - inverting the acceptance criterion.
risks.mitigation: Normalize to absent, then branch on absence: a blank or missing specialty calls the existing unnarrowed findAll path, and only a non-blank value reaches the narrowed query. The convention is shared with owner search; the code path is not.

risks.risk: Case-insensitive and whole-name-vs-prefix matching cannot be verified in VetControllerTests. That class is @WebMvcTest with a @MockitoBean VetRepository, so a stub returns whatever it was told to return regardless of the string passed. theVetDirectoryShouldMatchTheSpecialtyNameIgnoringCase and theVetDirectoryShouldNotMatchPartOfASpecialtyName would pass against an implementation that matches case-sensitively or by prefix - the semantics live in the generated SQL, not the controller.
risks.mitigation: Those two criteria need a repository-level test against the real H2 database and its seeded specialties (radiology, surgery, dentistry). The prd-entry's file_targets omits it; VetRepositoryTests is added to supporting_paths for that reason. The controller tests still carry their own share: that each surface passes the parameter to the narrowed method and the unnarrowed one when it is blank or absent.

risks.risk: The narrowed query is annotated @Cacheable("vets") to match its siblings. The cache key would then be caller-supplied, and the cache has no size limit and no eviction, so any caller can grow it without bound by sending distinct specialty values.
risks.mitigation: Do not annotate the narrowed methods. docs/adr/2026-08-26-uncached-request-narrowed-vet-queries.md records the decision and the rejected alternatives; the two existing findAll methods keep their annotations untouched so the no-parameter path is byte-for-byte today's behavior.

risks.risk: The specialty is reflected back into every pagination href. Built with the template's current string-preprocessing form (@{'/vets.html?page=__${i}__'}), a caller-supplied value would land in the URL literal unencoded.
risks.mitigation: Build the links as parameterized link expressions - @{/vets.html(page=${i}, specialty=${specialty})} - so Thymeleaf URL-encodes both values. This also yields the no-parameter case for free: Thymeleaf omits a null parameter, so with no specialty the links are exactly the URLs emitted today. The Threat Model XSS row in system-design.md now records this.

risks.risk: Vet.specialties is an EAGER @ManyToMany, so a narrowed query with a Pageable triggers Hibernate's in-memory pagination (HHH000104), as findAll(Pageable) already does.
risks.mitigation: Pre-existing and unchanged in kind; the seeded dataset is a handful of veterinarians. Do not switch the association to LAZY to avoid it - spring.jpa.open-in-view is disabled and the vet list template renders specialties, so a LAZY association would fail at render.

risks.risk: An empty result is treated the way OwnerController treats an empty owner search - rejectValue plus re-rendering the find form.
risks.mitigation: That behavior is owner-search-specific and REQ-VET-004 forbids it. A specialty no vet holds returns HTTP 200 with the normal page or document and an empty list, on both surfaces.

notes: Design constraints the implementer must honor, beyond the risks above. (1) The narrowing is a repository query, never an in-memory filter over findAll() in the controller. architecture-principles.md pattern catalog, Web controller row - a controller holds no business rule - and its checklist line: the existing controller-rule deviation does not extend to new rules. Normalizing a blank request parameter to absent is request adaptation and stays in the controller; selecting which vets match is data selection and belongs in the query. (2) Case folding goes in the query (an IgnoreCase derived-query keyword, generating a lower-cased comparison), not in the column collation. Leaving it to the column is exactly what makes the PostgreSQL owner search case-sensitive - system-design.md Known Defects - and would make the H2-only suite unable to observe the divergence. (3) Whole-name match: equality, not StartingWith. (4) Page size stays 5 and stays a local variable in the pagination helper, per the Constants section note. (5) The JSON surface stays unpaged and single-response per REQ-VET-003. (6) No form, dropdown, or link control is added to vetList.html - the hard boundary in the prd-entry non_goals and in the 2026-08-26 non-goal ADR, which records the visible control as an open question rather than a deferred part of the decision. Durable memory written this dispatch: docs/adr/2026-08-26-uncached-request-narrowed-vet-queries.md (new); docs/adr/README.md index rows for that ADR and for 2026-08-26-non-goal-vet-search-narrowed.md, which the product-requirements-expert could not add from its write scope; docs/system-design.md - Contracts Implements columns for Vets, VetRepository, VetController, removal of the stale Known Defects row about the machine-readable route, a Persistence paragraph on the two case-folding approaches, the Threat Model XSS row, and Open Question #5. No design-doc-autofix records exist in the log, so the autofix audit was a silent skip. Vocabulary is unchanged: Veterinarian and Specialty are already defined in docs/ubiquitous-language.md, and the Vets-the-wrapper versus vets-the-people caution there applies to prose about this slice.

author: code-quality-reviewer

findings.description: Local variable `namedSpecialty` is declared with the exact same name as the private method `namedSpecialty(String)` that produces it (`String namedSpecialty = namedSpecialty(specialty);`). Legal in Java, but a reader (or an IDE 'find usages' on the method) has to pause to disambiguate the call from the binding on the same line. `showResourcesVetList` avoids the issue by inlining the call instead of binding it.
findings.fix: Rename the local to something that isn't identical to the method identifier, e.g. `String specialtyFilter = namedSpecialty(specialty);` (and thread that name through to `findPaginated`/`addPaginationModel`).

approved_aspects: `namedSpecialty` is the single shared private helper feeding both routes (VetController.java:48,79,103) exactly as design-block line 10 requires — no blank-handling drift between the HTML and JSON surfaces.

Repository narrowing is a real derived query (`findBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase`), never an in-memory filter over `findAll()` in the controller — matches the architecture-principles controller-holds-no-business-rule constraint.

The two narrowed VetRepository methods are deliberately left off `@Cacheable("vets")` with a javadoc pointer to the ADR explaining why — verified against docs/adr/2026-08-26-uncached-request-narrowed-vet-queries.md and consistent with the two untouched `findAll` overloads.

vetList.html's per-href two-branch ternary (`${narrowed} ? @{...specialty=...} : @{...}`) matches the design-block's endorsed mechanism verbatim, including the explanatory comment; the rejected fragment-extraction alternative is correctly not present. No form/dropdown/control was added, honoring the hard boundary.

Methods stay small and single-purpose (`namedSpecialty`, `findPaginated`, `findVets`, `addPaginationModel`); javadoc on the new VetRepository methods matches the file's existing style and documents the case-folding and caching rationale.
checkFormat is clean; no unused imports, no swallowed exceptions, no raw System.out, no logging concerns in the changed surface.

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: Reflected XSS: all five pagination hrefs in src/main/resources/templates/vets/vetList.html (lines 39, 45, 51, 57, 63) are ternaries between two link expressions, @{/vets.html(page=..., specialty=${specialty})} and @{/vets.html(page=...)}, with narrowed hoisted onto the pagination div via th:with (line 34). The caller-supplied value is passed as a link-expression parameter, so Thymeleaf URL-encodes it and th:href HTML-escapes the attribute. The rejected mechanism is absent: swept the whole templates/ tree for th:utext and for @{__${...}__} preprocessing — zero hits anywhere, so the class has no other instance. No raw value reaches a URL literal or an unescaped output node.

XSS threat-model claim matches code: the extended Threat Model row in docs/system-design.md:183 describes exactly the delivered mechanism (link expressions, both branches, no string preprocessing, null-parameter rationale). Doc and code agree; no overclaim.

Injection: narrowing is Spring Data derived-query method naming (findBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase, VetRepository.java:78 and :89). Swept the vet package for @Query, createQuery, createNativeQuery, and string concatenation into query text - zero hits. No JPQL/SQL is assembled from the caller value; IgnoreCase folding is generated into the query rather than left to collation, which also keeps the comparison off vendor-specific paths.

Cache poisoning / unbounded key space: annotations match ADR docs/adr/2026-08-26-uncached-request-narrowed-vet-queries.md. @Cacheable("vets") appears on exactly the two unnarrowed reads (VetRepository.java:45, :55) and on neither caller-keyed method; grep for Cacheable across src/main/java returns only those two annotation sites plus the javadoc reference at :64. No caller-supplied value can reach a cache key.

Input normalization is single-sourced: VetController.namedSpecialty (VetController.java:104) strips and null-collapses, and both routes (/vets.html and /vets) normalize through it before dispatch, so the two surfaces cannot drift on what an empty value means. A null return provably reaches findAll rather than a whole-name match on the empty string.

Resource exhaustion on the unpaged JSON surface: an arbitrary caller-supplied filter value cannot enlarge the response - narrowing only ever returns a subset of the already-unpaged full vet list, so the worst case is the pre-existing unfiltered response. The value is bounded in practice by the container's query-string limit, is not persisted, is not logged, and is not a cache key, so an uncapped length carries no reachable amplification here. Noted, not raised as a finding.

Supply chain: no build file changed in the change set (build.gradle, settings.gradle, pom.xml all absent from scripts/changeset.sh --name-only), so no dependency was added, upgraded, or re-pointed and the dependency surface is byte-identical to the reviewed baseline.
